sections.title: Paul's Apostolic Authority and the Jerusalem Council
observations: In this section, Paul recounts his visit to Jerusalem to meet with the apostles. He emphasizes that his authority as an apostle comes directly from Christ, not from human sources. This is crucial for understanding the legitimacy of his message to the Galatians.

The meeting at Jerusalem was significant because it addressed the issue of whether Gentile believers needed to follow Jewish law. Paul stood firm in his conviction that salvation is by grace through faith, not by works of the law.

sections.title: The Confrontation with Peter
observations: Paul describes a confrontation with Peter (Cephas) in Antioch, where Peter withdrew from eating with Gentiles due to pressure from the circumcision group. This act was hypocritical and contrary to the gospel of grace.
Paul's public rebuke of Peter highlights the importance of living consistently with the truth of the gospel. It serves as a reminder that even leaders can falter and need correction.

importantVerses.commentary: A key verse that encapsulates the doctrine of justification by faith. Paul asserts that a person is justified not by works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ, emphasizing the core of the gospel message.

questions: What does Paul's defense of his apostolic authority teach us about the nature of divine calling?
How does the confrontation between Paul and Peter illustrate the challenges of maintaining gospel integrity in community?
In what ways can we apply the principle of justification by faith to our own lives and churches today?
